title: Would the band succeed later?
summary: It was of its time and he would not write for it again.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Do you think that if you had started Sauter-Finegan say twenty five years after you did, the climate today would be better for acceptance of the band?
I doubt it, because it was very much a part of its time, it wasn't ahead of its time or behind it; it was right then. It was a result of my reaction and Bill's reaction and all the

people in the band to the life around them. It grew out of that period, and you can reconstruct that period to a point, but you can never do the whole thing, you can never go the whole way. It becomes a facsimile somehow.
Would you still be interested in writing for that type of instrumentation?
You had your fill of it?

Yes. You have to have stimulus, you have to follow a need too, and that was the need at that time. It had something to do with my age too and my position in life, what was happening to me. None of that exists any longer. I don't have the energy I had then, although I didn't have that much energy then either.
over a long bout with TB.
There was a period between then when I had lots of energy. I don't worry about that anymore.
